logic.note: Angle = linear map of the HIGH pulse width (544 µs → 0°, 2400 µs → 180°, as the Arduino Servo library assumes). Pulses outside 400–2600 µs are ignored; with no pulses the horn holds where it is.

timing.note: Pulse width is measured from cycle-stamped pin edges (exact to one CPU cycle). The horn moves at the datasheet speed (0.1 s/60° at 4.8 V, scaled with voltage) in 1 ms steps; there is no acceleration, overshoot or deadband (real SG90 deadband ≈ 5–10 µs ≈ 1°).

analog.note: No position noise, gear backlash or load-dependent sag; under load the real horn droops a few degrees.

power.note: Supply current switches between 10 mA idle, 250 mA moving and 650 mA stalled (scaled with voltage), so supply sag on a shared 5 V rail shows up.

emulates: Travel speed (slew rate) and its voltage dependence
Mechanical end stops and stall current
doesNotEmulate: Torque limit under load (1.8 kg·cm) except a hard block
Behaviour with pulse rates far from 50 Hz
Unit-to-unit spread of the pulse range (many SG90s reach only ~170°)
testOnRealDevice: The real pulse range of your servo (end stops buzz when driven past them)
Brown-outs when several servos move at once on the Arduino 5 V (use a separate 5–6 V supply)
